reviewMethod: All 22 selected stored files across five current-corpus articles were independently rehashed against the fresh read-only GitHub evidence artifact, checked for exact task/page/article/source DOI binding, original Figure/Scheme identity and independent caption, captureVersion 6.2.20, job identity, fixed media generation 1790082000000, content-addressed R2 key, actual byte length/type/dimensions, duplicate source/hash ownership and current public media-index/ledger state. SVG files were parsed/rendered and checked for active/external content; PNG and WebP files were signature/decoding checked. Every image was visually reviewed against its caption and paper theme for role, unrelated/recommendation contamination, duplicate risk and legibility. Capture success/partial markers were treated only as provenance evidence. No publisher request, R2/D1 write, server-side direct import/repair, literature/card/title/scope mutation, userscript change or media-generation change was performed.
quality: The 22 files are exact stored bytes: 15 self-contained SVGs, two decoded PNGs and three decoded Nature WebPs plus two additional SVGs in the JOC set, all within the configured size bounds and with unique selected content/source ownership. None of the five DOI appears in the deployed body-publication ledger and no same-ID public body figure exists, so this packet is additive rather than a replacement. Existing official TOCs for the three Organic Letters papers are distinct and preserved. The JOC and Nature Chemistry records currently have no deployed TOC in the frozen public media index; the approved records remain body figures only and do not masquerade as TOC. JOC 10.1021/acs.joc.6c01498 has a final partial report of 7/8 body images, so only the seven exact stored files reviewed here are approved and the missing image is not inferred approved.
